units.text: Use CloudWatch Logs to collect, retain and work with events from applications or A W S services. A log group organizes streams and is where you set retention and access. Logs Insights queries the stored data; metric filters can feed alarms. Subscription filters send matching events to supported destinations. Check that the receiving system processes the records.

For continuous delivery to OpenSearch, choose the subscription path by latency and operations. The Lambda shipper gives you control of transformation and retry logic, but you own that work. Firehose buffers by time or size and has configured retry and failure-backup behavior. Test permissions, rejected documents, destination capacity and recovery in either design.

DocumentDB is a managed document database with selected MongoDB-compatible APIs. Here a compatible driver reaches the instance-based cluster, where the primary handles writes, read replicas can serve eligible reads, and distributed storage spans three Availability Zones. A W S manages storage, backups and monitoring. This is API compatibility, not a guarantee of identical behavior.

Follow a real application request into the target deployment before committing to migration. Check driver, authentication, certificate trust, query operators and indexes, then exercise the transactions the workload uses. Test failover and latency separately.

This picture shows an instance-based cluster; verify version and deployment-type support rather than treating the picture as a universal layout. For instance, compare the returned results and latency for a critical nested-document query on the current engine and the candidate. A successful connection cannot prove the query is equivalent.

For supported instance-based clusters, Standard bills separately for request I O along with instances and storage. I O-Optimized removes per-operation I O charges but uses different instance and storage pricing. Estimate spend using observed reads and writes, and include replica compute, backup storage and transfer. Use current Regional pricing; the best choice depends on workload.

A time-series record combines a timestamp, dimensions such as device or site, and a measured value. This makes a question like average temperature every fifteen minutes natural. Timestream for LiveAnalytics closed to new customers on June twentieth, twenty twenty-five. Evaluate Timestream for InfluxDB separately; it is a different engine and interface.

Follow the sensor observation into the database. The time tells you when it happened, the dimensions tell you where or for which device, and the measures hold temperature or vibration. Filter a time window and group by the dimensions you care about. Design for that aggregation rather than borrowing an unrelated document-key access pattern.

Track one sensor event through the stream, transform and time-series database into a query. A producer acknowledgement only proves the first step. Verify accepted writes and query the expected window. Check late arrivals, duplicates, retention and failed-record handling.

The illustrated path is conceptual; use the supported writer and API for the selected engine. For the drill, resend one event, deliver another late, then compare the resulting count and average with a known expected result. This checks the actual consumer rather than just ingestion throughput.

In a sandbox, create a table with partition and sort keys. Add the two game records, then query user forty-two with the game prefix. Compare a Scan and measure actual consumed capacity and pagination. For lookup by game ID, add the global secondary index, wait for Active, and verify the eventual read separately. The table query answers which games belong to the user; the index answers which records match a game ID. Neither successful test proves the other path.

A recovery drill proves the workload, not just the backup. Select the authorized snapshot or restore point and confirm engine and key access. Restore a new private instance with the intended network configuration. Connect, validate representative data and app operations, then switch only the sandbox endpoint and measure the time. Keep a rollback decision ready.

Use a bounded sandbox burst to check whether RDS Proxy reduces database connection pressure. Keep the database private, configure the supported authentication, and compare client connections with database connections and borrow latency. Look for session pinning rather than expecting one database connection. Try a denied sandbox client as a negative test, then clean up.

Request product forty-two twice. The first miss reads version one from the database and fills the cache; the next request hits. Update the source to version two and observe the old cached value until invalidation or expiry. Refresh and verify version two, then safely test the sandbox fallback when the cache is unavailable.
